guarantees.claim: The function valid_chk always returns the bitwise reduction-OR of value AND (NOT reduction-AND of value), i.e., true if value has at least one 1 and at least one 0, false otherwise.

assumptions.claim: The caller must supply a value argument of width exactly MaxWidth.
assumptions.risk: If a value of different width is passed, implicit truncation or zero-extension could cause the function to evaluate incorrect bits, potentially missing an all-zero or all-one pattern for the intended data.

uncertain_points.claim: The function rejects all‑zero and all‑one vectors but accepts any other pattern, including those with very low Hamming weight or symmetric patterns that may still be cryptographically weak. The design intent of this check is unclear.
uncertain_points.cond: when the function result is used to qualify key/entropy data
uncertain_points.risk: Weak key material (e.g., 000…001 or 111…110) could be accepted, potentially violating a security requirement that expects stronger randomness checks.
